parentLift.note: Leg drive moves more weight than a strict press, so it counts at three quarters.

tagline: Dip, drive with the legs, and send it overhead.

coaching.summary: With the bar resting on the front of your shoulders, dip a few inches at the knees, drive up hard with the legs, and press the bar overhead to lockout.
cues: Dip straight down a few inches with the torso upright and heels planted.
Reverse the dip fast so the legs launch the bar off the shoulders.
Press through to lockout with the bar over the middle of the foot.

standardsRef.note: Leg drive lets most lifters push press about a fifth more than they press.

introduction.title: What the Push Press Builds
paragraphs: The push press is an overhead press that starts with your legs. With the bar on the front of your shoulders, you dip a few inches at the knees, drive up hard, and let that drive launch the bar so your arms can finish the press to lockout.

The leg drive lets you put more weight overhead than you can press strictly, usually about a fifth more. That builds power from the ground up, strong shoulders and triceps at lockout, and confidence holding heavy weight overhead.

Keep your torso upright and your heels down in the dip, and reverse it fast. The bar should **leave your shoulders from the leg drive** before your arms take over. Sets of 3 to 5 reps suit most lifters.
Log your push presses and this page charts your rep PRs and tonnage, ready to read beside your [strict press](/progress-guide/strict-press).

faqItems.question: What is the difference between a push press and a strict press?
faqItems.answer: A strict press uses only the upper body, with the knees locked from start to finish. A push press adds a short dip and drive from the legs to get the bar moving. See the [strict press guide](/progress-guide/strict-press) for the stricter lift.

faqItems.question: How much more can I push press than strict press?
faqItems.answer: Most lifters push press about 20 percent more than they strict press. The better your timing between the leg drive and the press, the bigger that gap can be.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between a push press and a push jerk?
faqItems.answer: In a push press your legs straighten once and stay straight while your arms finish the lift. In a [push jerk](/progress-guide/push-jerk) you bend your knees a second time to drop under the bar and catch it on locked arms.

faqItems.question: How deep should the dip be?
faqItems.answer: Shallow, only a few inches. A short, quick dip with an upright torso sends the bar straight up. A deep, slow dip turns it into a squat and takes the snap out of the drive.

faqItems.question: Does the push press help my strict press?
faqItems.answer: It helps many lifters, because it gets you used to heavier weight overhead and strengthens the top half of the press. Train both and watch them rise together.

faqItems.question: How often should I push press?
faqItems.answer: Once a week works well, either after your strict press or on a separate overhead day.
